QUOTE: "`MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member)` is a rename, not access control... Outside code that writes `ctx->alg` gets a compile error. The struct definitions stay in public headers, so `sizeof`, stack allocation and layout are still visible."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states that opacity is enforced at compile time by renaming members (so the old names fail to compile) while the struct layout and size stay visible.
